## 1. Online Order Amounts

A retailer wants to know the average amount its online customers spend per order. It looks at 450 orders, and the average of those orders was \$85.37.

## 1. Online Order Amounts

A retailer wants to know the average amount its online customers spend per order. It looks at 450 orders, and the average of those orders was \$85.37.

|  | Size | Mean |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Population | ? | ? |
| Sample | ? | ? |

What is the sample size?

What is the sample mean?

## 1. Online Order Amounts

A retailer wants to know the average amount its online customers spend per order. It looks at 450 orders, and the average of those orders was \$85.37.

|  | Size | Mean |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Population | ? | ? |
| Sample | 450 | \$85.37 |

The population mean $\mu$ is unknown, but the sample mean is $\bar{x} = \$85.37$.

## 5. Sustainable Clothing Spending

A market research firm wants to know the average amount adult shoppers in the United States spend on sustainable clothing each year. The firm interviews 500 adult shoppers, and the average reported spending was \$122.64.
